This website aims to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA, in Arabic as fully as in English.

Last reviewed: 17 October 2026

We want everyone who reads HAYKALAH’s website, on a phone or a desktop, in Arabic or in English, to be able to use it. This statement sets out our target, what we have done, what we know still needs work and how to tell us about a barrier.

01Our target

Our target is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA, in both languages. The Arabic site is not a lesser copy: every page is published in Arabic and English, with the same content.

02What we have done

  • Two languages, one site. Every page exists in Arabic and English, and you can switch language from any page. The page’s language is declared, so screen readers use the right voice.
  • Right-to-left layout. Arabic pages are fully mirrored, and numbers and Latin names are set so that they read in the right order inside Arabic text.
  • Keyboard access. Menus, forms, the cookie banner and other controls work with a keyboard, and focus is always visible.
  • Contrast. Text meets AA contrast, including on the dark theme and where text sits over photographs.
  • Reduced motion. If your device asks for reduced motion, movement is removed and only short fades remain. Nothing on the site flashes.
  • The hero video. It is muted, has a visible pause control and never sits behind small text. With reduced motion on, a still image is shown instead.
  • Captions and text alternatives. Meaningful images have text alternatives, and figures and charts carry written captions. The hero video has no sound or speech.
  • Forms. Every field has a visible label, required fields are marked, and error messages say what to correct.
  • Structure. Each page has one main heading and a logical heading order, and the site works from phone width to large screens without sideways scrolling.

03Known limitations

If you find a barrier, please tell us and we will fix it.

Items we are checking:

  • The credentials pack PDF in English and Arabic.
  • Ask HAYKALAH (Beta), including how answers are announced to screen readers.
  • Interactive tools: the Structure Finder, the explainers, the Signature work explorer and the asset readiness check.

04Report a barrier

If something on the site is hard or impossible for you to use, please tell us at haykalah@haykalah.com. It helps if you include:

  • the page address;
  • what you were trying to do;
  • your device, browser and any assistive technology you use.

A member of the team will reply by email.

05How we test

Pages are checked at phone and desktop widths in both languages, with the keyboard, and against AA contrast. An independent accessibility review is planned; we will publish its results here.

07Questions

Can I turn off the movement on the site?

Yes. Turn on “reduce motion” in your device or browser settings, and the site removes movement and shows a still image in place of the hero video. You can also pause the video with its own control.

Is the Arabic site the same as the English site?

Yes. Every page is published in both languages with the same content, and the Arabic pages read from right to left.
